messages:
april: flagging risk: during prefix handoff we saw observed spikes in DB fetches in the last rehearsal. need a safer handshake to avoid double-fetch and stale writes. thoughts on a lightweight protocol?
vikram: agree. heavy 2PC is overkill. propose a 3-state lifecycle: ACTIVE -> HANDOFF_PENDING -> HANDOFF_COMPLETED. move nodes coordinate by publishing a transfer_epoch + nonce.
maria: so entries carry (transfer_epoch, nonce, state). read path checks epoch and acts accordingly. if req.epoch < entry.transfer_epoch -> do shadow fetch.
lee: detail: we should prefer nonblocking demote: on HANDOFF_PENDING mark entry as "read-OK write-probe" meaning reads return cached but writes validate nonce. that prevents stale writes landing.
cal: for write validation pseudo: ```
if entry.state == "HANDOFF_PENDING":
  if write.nonce != entry.nonce:
    return 409, {"Retry-After": "1s", "PF-Transfer-Epoch": entry.transfer_epoch}
  else:
    apply_write()
```
april: good. also important: when host A starts handoff it should soft-demote rather than delete. soft-demote: set promotable=false, ttl=shorten(10s) and push to soft-evict queue. that avoids two hosts actively promoting the same prefix.
vikram: soft-evict queue length is a control signal. if it grows > threshold we should slow migration rate. emit metric pf.soft_demote_queue_len and pf.handoff_throttle_count.
maria: we need a clear TTL policy: keep soft-demoted entry for min(remaining_ttl, 30s) to give other node time to observe. if expiration happens, the new owner will fetch once and then promote.
lee: multi-key operations: we can't guarantee atomic visibility if different keys transfer at different times. mitigation: advertise transfer windows in meta and delay large transactions crossing transferred prefixes. ops will retry on 409s with backoff.
cal: add client header PF-Transfer-Nonce and PF-Transfer-Epoch for writes so client SDKs can surface helpful errors. lower-level runtimes can auto-retry when they see 409+Retry-After.
april: rollout plan: 1) unit tests and integration harness 2) dogfood in staging with artificial churn 3) feature-flagged canary (start with 3 tenants) 4) monitor for 60m windows: shadow_reads, transfer_conflicts, soft_demote_backlog, write_reject_rate 5) ramp or rollback. thresholds: write_reject_rate > 0.3% for 10m -> rollback.
vikram: testing matrix: chaos test with concurrent handoff + eviction + hotkeys; correctness test for nonce mismatch path; stress test measuring DB QPS during handoff. I'll own stress harness.
maria: I'll own the RFC and provide full state transition diagrams + lifecycle table. also include the exact header names we publish: PF-Transfer-Epoch, PF-Transfer-Nonce.
lee: implementer note: make the transfer_epoch monotonic and embedded in handoff id (epoch<<32 | nonce). simplifies comparisons.
cal: ops: expose a /handoff/status endpoint that shows current transfers and soft_demote_queue lengths, so SRE can respond quickly.
infra-bot: created feature-flag prefetched_handoff_handshake (owners: @april, @maria). initial rollout: 3 tenants in dev, 3 in staging.
april: one more safety: when a node receives a write with missing PF-Transfer-Epoch header, treat it as epoch 0 and validate against entry. this stops unsafeguarded clients from accidentally overwriting a handoff. we should surface SDK updates.
vikram: agree. also capture metrics per-tenant: pf.transfer_conflicts_by_tenant so we can pause churny customers.
maria: ok i'll draft RFC + sample code and link PRs. anyone want to coauthor?
lee: happy to do the correctness and tests sections.
cal: i'll add ops runbook.
april: thanks all — closing thread, will post RFC link and the test checklist shortly.
